;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[2018–19 Iraqi protests]], [[October 2019 Iraqi protests]]
**Fifteen more people are killed in clashes between security forces and protestors in [[Iraq]], raising the overall death toll to 222 since protests began this month. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/10/killed-iraq-anti-government-protests-continue-191026155414026.html (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-iraq-protests/fifteen-killed-dozens-wounded-as-iraq-protests-flare-for-second-day-idUSKBN1X507K (Reuters)]
**[[Prime Minister of Iraq|Prime Minister]] [[Adil Abdul-Mahdi]] orders the [[Iraqi Special Operations Forces|elite Counter-Terrorism Service]] to quell the protests in the capital [[Baghdad]] and the southern city of [[Nasiriya]]. [https://www.voanews.com/middle-east/nearly-50-dead-iraq-protests-take-new-violent-turn (Voice of America)]
*[[2019 Turkish offensive into north-eastern Syria]], [[Second Northern Syria Buffer Zone]]
**[[Government of Turkey|Turkish]] [[Minister of Foreign Affairs (Turkey)|Foreign Minister]] [[Mevlüt Çavuşoğlu]] rejects a proposal by [[Government of Germany|German]] [[Federal Ministry of Defence (Germany)|Defence Minister]] [[Annegret Kramp-Karrenbauer]] to establish a [[United Nations]]-mandated security zone in northeastern [[Syria]], calling the plan "not very realistic". [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/10/turkey-rejects-german-security-zone-plan-unrealistic-191026141506342.html (Al Jazeera)]  
*Sea-Eye, a charity which performs migrant rescue operations in the [[Mediterranean Sea]], claims the [[Libya]]n [[coastguard]] circled their ship MV ''Alan Kurdi'' and fired warning shots into the air, with weapons pointed at crew and the migrants they were rescuing. [https://www.dw.com/en/libya-authorities-fire-warning-shots-at-migrant-rescue-ship/a-51001668 (Deutsche Welle)]
;Disasters and accidents
*Flooding in [[Japan]] kills nine people in [[Chiba Prefecture|Chiba]] and one more in [[Fukushima Prefecture|Fukushima]], with a further person missing in the latter. [https://gulfnews.com/world/asia/flood-mudslides-from-heavy-rain-in-japan-kill-at-least-10-1.67408304 (''Gulf News'')]
;Business and economy
*''[[The Times]]'' reports that the [[David and Frederick Barclay|Barclay family]] is looking to sell ''[[The Daily Telegraph]]'' and ''[[The Sunday Telegraph]]'', citing conflicting viewpoints within the family and low circulation. The ''[[Daily Mail]]'', [[Amazon (company)|Amazon]] CEO [[Jeff Bezos]], and ''[[Evening Standard]]'' owner [[Evgeny Lebedev]] are rumored to be potential buyers. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-britain-divestiture-telegraph/barclay-family-puts-telegraph-newspapers-up-for-sale-the-times-idUKKBN1X42IE (Reuters)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-50192912 (BBC News)]

;Law and crime
*[[Trial of Catalonia independence leaders]]; [[2019 Catalan protests]]
**In a demonstration in [[Barcelona]], 350,000 people protest prison sentences given to Catalan leaders. The protest turns violent with clashes with [[National Police Corps]] and [[Mossos d'Esquadra]]. [https://www.euronews.com/2019/10/26/catalonia-braces-for-more-protests-as-separatists-set-to-rally-in-barcelona (Euronews)] [https://www.lavanguardia.com/politica/20191026/471203818849/manifestacion-independentista-barcelona-26-octubre-contra-sentencia-juicio-proces-via-laietana-calle-marina-en-directo.html (''La Vanguardia'')]
*[[2019 Grays incident]]
**The driver of the lorry in which 39 bodies were found is charged with 39 counts of [[manslaughter in English law|manslaughter]], as well as [[immigration to the United Kingdom|immigration offences]], [[money laundering]], and [[people trafficking]]. Three other people remain in police custody suspected of manslaughter and people trafficking after 39 bodies were found in a lorry earlier this week. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-essex-50196265 (BBC News)]
